reason: Driven and verified verbatim. Loading state=owner-draft renders 'Only you can see this', the verb 'Publish', stamp 'Updated 16 July 2026'. Pressing Publish lands on .b-pressTitle = 'Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July.' with the .b-live strap announcing 'The link is below.' Pressing 'Back to the plan' returns 'Live since 15 July · anyone with the link can read it' and rolls the stamp back to 'Updated 15 July 2026'. So a plan nobody holds becomes a plan held the day before today, and the footer's time runs backwards, in two clicks. The stated cause is correct: render-b.js:1429-1435 stashes F.publication/F.updatedLabel, renders the draft branch, then restores the fixture's published record, so states.publish (render-b.js:1631) and the SAID.publish strap (render-b.js:1302) read the published record the state was built to contradict. The gates do not cover it: interaction-check.mjs never loads owner-draft, and its only publication assertion ('the publish verb knows whether anyone is holding a copy', line 2596) tests the verb on the fixture's published record. Answering the panel's question directly: the contradiction fires ONLY from the synthetic owner-draft state. The real first-run path is clean — owner-empty, set the day, Add a moment gives 'Only you can see this' / 'Publish' / 'Updated 16 July 2026', and Publish from there lands on 'Send it to Aisling & Tom.' with 'Ready to send. The link is below.' That means the fix is a state-builder fix, not a copy or logic fix. I simulated the proposed change in-page (leave the draft record in place after the builder) and it produces exactly the claimed result: 'Send it to Mara & Finn.', 'Ready to send. The link is below.', and a consistent return to 'Only you can see this' with the stamp at 16 July. It also matches the precedent already in the file: the owner-empty first-run path (render-b.js:1481) sets the same draft record and deliberately does NOT restore it. Confirmed, but the fix as written is half right: its predicted after-Copy flip does not happen. Measured, pressing 'Copy the link' on the publish screen flips nothing — on the real first-run path the heading stays 'Send it to Aisling & Tom.' and 'Back to the plan' still reads 'Only you can see this' with the verb still 'Publish'. The transition the fix relies on (F.publication = { state: 'published', publishedAt: F.today } at render-b.js:1156) sits in wireOwner's click handler, and no data-act="copy" control exists anywhere on the owner surface — the only 'Copy the link' is in states.publish (render-b.js:1659), whose own handler (render-b.js:1666-1685) sets the button label and the live line and never touches the record. So the flip is unreachable dead code today, and 'Taking the link IS the publish in this model' is a comment the artifact does not honour on either path.
sharpenedFix: Two edits in render-b.js, both in the source that build.mjs generates master.html from. (1) In states["owner-draft"] (line 1429), drop the stash/restore: set F.publication = { state: "draft", publishedAt: null } and F.updatedLabel = F.fmt.medium(F.today) + " " + F.fmt.year(F.today) before ownerSurface({}) and leave them set, exactly as the owner-empty first-run path at line 1481 already does, with the same comment reason. (2) Move the publication flip that is currently stranded in wireOwner (lines 1153-1158) into the states.publish copy handler, inside the clipboard success callback beside action.textContent = "Copied": if (F.publication.state !== "published") { F.publication = { state: "published", publishedAt: F.today }; } and repaint the press heading from the same record (node.querySelector('.b-pressTitle') text), so the heading flips to 'Mara & Finn have had this since 16 July.' in place; paintPublication() already exists and will do the owner surface's status line, verb and stamp on the next go("owner-flight"). Delete the now-duplicated dead branch in wireOwner so there is one writer, not two. After both edits: owner-draft reads 'Only you can see this' / 'Publish' / 'Updated 16 July 2026'; Publish lands on 'Send it to Mara & Finn.' with 'Ready to send. The link is below.'; Copy the link makes it 'Mara & Finn have had this since 16 July.'; Back to the plan reads 'Live since 16 July · anyone with the link can read it' with the stamp still at 16 July. Watch one consequence when re-running: the console (console.html) switches state in-page without a reload, so the un-restored record persists across a state change made from the picker — the same leak the owner-empty path already produces, and worth scoping by resetting the record in C.setState rather than by restoring it inside the builder.
